intro_html: Meatballs and marinara without spending your evening rolling and frying. Cooked skillet-style, this lean turkey pasta delivers 57 grams of protein per serving for about $5.04 (at everyday cost), and it stretches to 14 servings. That is Italian night on repeat for the price of one takeout order.
cost_closing_html: About $5.04 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Every one of the 14 servings packs 57 grams of protein and 654 calories, so it fuels you like a full plate should.
upsell_html: Comfort-food Italian, meal-prepped and budget-approved. Twirl your fork and enjoy. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Jarred marinara on sale is cheaper and faster than building sauce from scratch, and three jars cover the whole batch.
A wedge or tub of real parmesan goes a long way. A little grated over the top does more work than a lot of the pre-shredded blends.
Buy pasta when it drops to a dollar a box and stock the pantry. It keeps forever and this recipe leans on it.
make_it: Brown 6.9 pounds of 93/7 ground turkey with the chopped onion and a splash of olive oil, breaking it into meatball-sized chunks.
Boil the penne separately until just tender, then drain.
Pour the marinara over the turkey and let it simmer so the sauce soaks in.
Toss the cooked pasta into the sauce until everything is coated.
Finish each container with a shower of parmesan while it is still hot.
